active_problem.requested_solution: Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills (CL-01, requested by SH-CS).
symptoms: Monthly dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600 (Jun-Jul) to 1180-1260 (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-05).
Manual-read route completion is 12 points below target (88% vs 95%) for 9200 accounts, Aug-Sep 2026 (E-01).
41% of currently disputed bills (1240/3025) used ESTIMATED reads versus 59% (1785/3025) ACTUAL reads (E-03).
active_problem.root_problem: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled since August 2026 (610/month Jun to 1180-1260/month Aug-Sep, E-05). A confirmed contributing mechanism: manual-read route completion fell to 88% against a 95% target for 9200 accounts over Aug-Sep (E-01), pushing more accounts onto estimate substitution, which accounts for 41% (1240/3025) of currently disputed bills (E-03). Tariff changes (E-02) and dispute-handling capacity (E-04, within SLA) are ruled out as causes, but this estimate-substitution mechanism does not yet explain the majority (59%, 1785/3025) of disputed bills, which used ACTUAL reads (E-03) — a second, unconfirmed billing-pipeline mechanism is driving most of the surge.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Field route completion for manual-read accounts was 88% against a 95% target over Aug-Sep 2026, covering 9200 accounts — a measurable shortfall in completed manual reads during the dispute-surge period.
The billing system's tariff change log shows zero records, meaning no tariff rate changes occurred in the reviewed period that could explain higher bill amounts driving the dispute surge.

Among disputed bills, 1785 (59%) used ACTUAL meter reads and 1240 (41%) used ESTIMATED reads (total 3025), so the majority of disputes attach to bills that were NOT estimate-substituted. This means read-estimate failures (AMI delivery or field-read gaps) explain at most a minority of disputed bills; something else is driving disputes on bills with ACTUAL reads too.

CRM dispute response-time data (2440 tickets, median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days, SLA 3.0 days) shows tickets are currently being resolved within SLA despite the volume surge, so ticket-handling capacity/speed is not currently failing. This weighs against the surge being explained by handling capacity not scaling, pointing instead toward volume/cause-of-disputes as the driver.

CRM data shows monthly dispute counts of 610 (Jun), 590 (Jul), 1180 (Aug), 1260 (Sep) — confirming that ticket volume roughly doubled abruptly between July and August, matching the stakeholder's claimed timing but adding no information about cause.

This is an unverified, non-authoritative explanation offered for the route-completion shortfall already measured in F-01/E-01, but it only speaks to the estimate-substitution channel and says nothing about disputes on bills with ACTUAL reads (E-03), which form the majority of disputes.

active_problem.root_problem: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled since August 2026 (610/590 per month Jun/Jul to 1180/1260 Aug/Sep, E-05), driven by billing-import validation rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01, E-12), which compares raw AMI register values to 12-month m3 consumption history with no unit scaling. Because AMI meters on firmware v4.2 (rolled out June 2026, E-13) report register values in 0.1 m3 instead of m3, BV-17 systematically misflags high consumption at import. This is confirmed for the ESTIMATED-read channel, where 1184 of 1240 disputed bills had a valid AMI read rejected by billing import for high consumption rather than lacking a read at all (E-11); because BV-17 applies at import regardless of read channel (E-12), the same mechanism plausibly also explains disputes on the dominant ACTUAL-read channel (59%, 1785/3025, E-03). Tariff changes (E-02, E-06) and ticket-handling capacity (E-04, within SLA) are ruled out as causes.

release_summary.summary: The customer-service request (CL-01: tickets doubled, build an AI agent to auto-answer and fix wrong bills) was treated as a claim to investigate, not an instruction. Evidence ruled out tariff changes (E-02, E-06) and ticket-handling capacity (E-04) as causes of the doubling (E-05). An initial hypothesis that field-reader staffing shortfalls (E-01, E-07) drove estimate-substitution disputes was invalidated once E-11 showed most 'estimated-read' disputed bills actually had valid AMI reads that were rejected at billing import for high consumption. Combined with the discovery of validation rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01, E-12) and a firmware unit mismatch on v4.2 meters (E-13), the problem was redefined (PD-1@v2) as a billing-import unit-scaling defect, confirmed for the ESTIMATED-read channel but only hypothesized (not yet directly confirmed) for the larger ACTUAL-read channel (59% of disputes). The system released RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION: it delivers the confirmed billing-validation-rule-log finding (E-12/F-09) as the EXECUTE deliverable for the sole in-scope item, but does not fix the BV-17 defect (infeasible given read-only tooling), does not confirm the mechanism for ACTUAL-read disputes, does not validate the success metric, and does not resolve who would execute a remedy or review already-issued incorrect bills — all tracked as open verification obligations and explicit known limitations rather than resolved items."
key_points: Problem as defined (PD-1@v2, DEFINE gate CONDITIONAL_PASS): dispute tickets roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to 1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-05). Root cause identified as billing-import validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 (E-12), which compares raw AMI register values to 12-month m3 history with no unit scaling; AMI meters on firmware v4.2 (rolled out June 2026) report register values in 0.1 m3 instead of m3 (E-13), so BV-17 systematically misflags high consumption at import.

This mechanism is directly confirmed only for the ESTIMATED-read dispute channel: 1184 of 1240 ESTIMATED disputed bills had a valid AMI read received and exported, but it was rejected by billing import for high consumption rather than missing (E-11), not the lack-of-read story originally assumed.

The original problem definition (PD-1@v1) attributed the surge to field route-completion shortfall (88% vs 95% target, E-01) feeding estimate substitution; this was invalidated when E-11 showed the rejected-AMI-read mechanism instead, triggering a full dependency review (DR-1) that invalidated the first solution design, remedies and several work items.

Tariff changes (E-02, E-06) and ticket-handling capacity (E-04, within SLA) were ruled out as causes. BV-17 applying 'at import regardless of read channel' (E-12) makes it a plausible explanation for the dominant ACTUAL-read channel too (59% of disputes, E-03), but this is not yet directly confirmed on ACTUAL-read accounts.

Release decision: RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION, with no holds. The release delivers the confirmed billing-validation-rule-log finding (E-12/F-09, BV-17) as the EXECUTE-phase deliverable for the sole release-scope item query_billing_validation_rule_log:DA-RULES.

The release does not fix BV-17 itself: that remedy (firmware-aware unit scaling) is marked infeasible in contest time because billing-config is read-only in the tool surface, and any bill-write correction would require SH-BILL's K-BILLWRITE authority, which this release does not exercise.

Three verification obligations remain open and are explicitly outside this release's scope: whether ACTUAL-read disputes show the same AMI-rejection pattern (VOB-U-AMI-READ-ACCURACY-FOR-ACTUAL), whether raw dispute-volume reduction validly reflects bill-accuracy improvement versus faster ticket closure (VOB-U-SUCCESS-METRIC-VALIDITY), and who/what process would execute the BV-17 fix (VOB-U-REMEDY-EXECUTION-PATH).

The original stakeholder-requested solution ('AI agent that auto-answers tickets and fixes whatever is causing wrong bills', CL-01) was not what was delivered; the investigation treated that request as an unverified claim to test, and the handling-capacity hypothesis behind it (H-RESPONSE-HANDLING-GAP) was rejected by E-04.
limitations_explained: Does not confirm root cause for ACTUAL-read disputes (59% of disputes, E-03): the query needed to check AMI read events on ACTUAL-channel accounts (query_ami_read_events:DA-MDMS) remains blocked by the open VOB-U-AMI-READ-ACCURACY-FOR-ACTUAL, so the BV-17 mechanism is only proven for the ESTIMATED channel, not the majority ACTUAL channel.

No formal root-cause-and-fix document was produced, because document_root_cause_and_recommend_fix:DA-RULES is blocked by the open VOB-U-REMEDY-EXECUTION-PATH, which asks who/what process would implement a BV-17 or firmware-scaling correction given billing-config is read-only and K-BILLWRITE forbids automated bill writes.

It cannot be validated whether any future reduction in raw dispute-ticket volume would reflect true bill-accuracy improvement or merely faster/automated ticket closure, since VOB-U-SUCCESS-METRIC-VALIDITY (blocking analyze_disputed_bills_by_read_type) is still open; any observed volume drop is corroborated by a bill-accuracy indicator only, not attributable to ticket handling alone.

The underlying BV-17 unit-scaling defect itself is not fixed by this release: SR-R-FIX-BV17-UNIT-SCALING is marked infeasible in contest time because the billing-config tool surface is read-only, so no corrective change to the rule could be executed.

Bills already issued incorrectly under BV-17 still require Billing Operations (SH-BILL) to review and credit/re-bill them under the K-BILLWRITE authority constraint; this release performs no such write and does not perform that review.

The DEFINE gate result for this problem definition was CONDITIONAL_PASS, meaning some items (the three open VOBs above) were deferred rather than resolved before release, by explicit design of the gate process, not by oversight.

key_points: Problem as defined (PD-1@v2, DEFINE gate CONDITIONAL_PASS): dispute tickets roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to 1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-05). Root cause identified as billing-import validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 (E-12), which compares raw AMI register values to 12-month m3 history with no unit scaling; AMI meters on firmware v4.2 (rolled out June 2026) report register values in 0.1 m3 instead of m3 (E-13), so BV-17 systematically misflags high consumption at import.

This mechanism is directly confirmed only for the ESTIMATED-read dispute channel: 1184 of 1240 ESTIMATED disputed bills had a valid AMI read received and exported, but it was rejected by billing import for high consumption rather than missing (E-11), not the lack-of-read story originally assumed.

The original problem definition (PD-1@v1) attributed the surge to field route-completion shortfall (88% vs 95% target, E-01) feeding estimate substitution; this was invalidated when E-11 showed the rejected-AMI-read mechanism instead, triggering a full dependency review (DR-1) that invalidated the first solution design, remedies and several work items.

Tariff changes (E-02, E-06) and ticket-handling capacity (E-04, within SLA) were ruled out as causes. BV-17 applying 'at import regardless of read channel' (E-12) makes it a plausible explanation for the dominant ACTUAL-read channel too (59% of disputes, E-03), but this is not yet directly confirmed on ACTUAL-read accounts.

Release decision: RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION, with no holds. The release delivers the confirmed billing-validation-rule-log finding (E-12/F-09, BV-17) as the EXECUTE-phase deliverable for the sole release-scope item query_billing_validation_rule_log:DA-RULES.

The release does not fix BV-17 itself: that remedy (firmware-aware unit scaling) is marked infeasible in contest time because billing-config is read-only in the tool surface, and any bill-write correction would require SH-BILL's K-BILLWRITE authority, which this release does not exercise.

Three verification obligations remain open and are explicitly outside this release's scope: whether ACTUAL-read disputes show the same AMI-rejection pattern (VOB-U-AMI-READ-ACCURACY-FOR-ACTUAL), whether raw dispute-volume reduction validly reflects bill-accuracy improvement versus faster ticket closure (VOB-U-SUCCESS-METRIC-VALIDITY), and who/what process would execute the BV-17 fix (VOB-U-REMEDY-EXECUTION-PATH).

The original stakeholder-requested solution ('AI agent that auto-answers tickets and fixes whatever is causing wrong bills', CL-01) was not what was delivered; the investigation treated that request as an unverified claim to test, and the handling-capacity hypothesis behind it (H-RESPONSE-HANDLING-GAP) was rejected by E-04.
limitations_explained: Does not confirm root cause for ACTUAL-read disputes (59% of disputes, E-03): the query needed to check AMI read events on ACTUAL-channel accounts (query_ami_read_events:DA-MDMS) remains blocked by the open VOB-U-AMI-READ-ACCURACY-FOR-ACTUAL, so the BV-17 mechanism is only proven for the ESTIMATED channel, not the majority ACTUAL channel.

No formal root-cause-and-fix document was produced, because document_root_cause_and_recommend_fix:DA-RULES is blocked by the open VOB-U-REMEDY-EXECUTION-PATH, which asks who/what process would implement a BV-17 or firmware-scaling correction given billing-config is read-only and K-BILLWRITE forbids automated bill writes.

It cannot be validated whether any future reduction in raw dispute-ticket volume would reflect true bill-accuracy improvement or merely faster/automated ticket closure, since VOB-U-SUCCESS-METRIC-VALIDITY (blocking analyze_disputed_bills_by_read_type) is still open; any observed volume drop is corroborated by a bill-accuracy indicator only, not attributable to ticket handling alone.

The underlying BV-17 unit-scaling defect itself is not fixed by this release: SR-R-FIX-BV17-UNIT-SCALING is marked infeasible in contest time because the billing-config tool surface is read-only, so no corrective change to the rule could be executed.

Bills already issued incorrectly under BV-17 still require Billing Operations (SH-BILL) to review and credit/re-bill them under the K-BILLWRITE authority constraint; this release performs no such write and does not perform that review.

The DEFINE gate result for this problem definition was CONDITIONAL_PASS, meaning some items (the three open VOBs above) were deferred rather than resolved before release, by explicit design of the gate process, not by oversight.
output.summary: The customer-service request (CL-01: tickets doubled, build an AI agent to auto-answer and fix wrong bills) was treated as a claim to investigate, not an instruction. Evidence ruled out tariff changes (E-02, E-06) and ticket-handling capacity (E-04) as causes of the doubling (E-05). An initial hypothesis that field-reader staffing shortfalls (E-01, E-07) drove estimate-substitution disputes was invalidated once E-11 showed most 'estimated-read' disputed bills actually had valid AMI reads that were rejected at billing import for high consumption. Combined with the discovery of validation rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01, E-12) and a firmware unit mismatch on v4.2 meters (E-13), the problem was redefined (PD-1@v2) as a billing-import unit-scaling defect, confirmed for the ESTIMATED-read channel but only hypothesized (not yet directly confirmed) for the larger ACTUAL-read channel (59% of disputes). The system released RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION: it delivers the confirmed billing-validation-rule-log finding (E-12/F-09) as the EXECUTE deliverable for the sole in-scope item, but does not fix the BV-17 defect (infeasible given read-only tooling), does not confirm the mechanism for ACTUAL-read disputes, does not validate the success metric, and does not resolve who would execute a remedy or review already-issued incorrect bills — all tracked as open verification obligations and explicit known limitations rather than resolved items."
